text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT fired for service `inference-proxy` (critical) — INC12345 — reason: `proxy_latency_p95 > 800ms` (3/5 windows). Link: https://pagerduty.company/INC12345 :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): acked — I'm on it. Assigning to myself. Notifying SRE. :hand:

ben (sre): looking at metrics now. preliminary: 1m p95 spike at 14:03 UTC, then dropped. scaling activity around same time. grabbing autoscaler events and proxy logs.

carol (platform): saw a brief GPU pool reshuffle in the region at ~14:02, could be related. No capacity errors in cluster events.

alice (oncall): copying logs, running quick health checks: `curl -sS https://proxy.service/health | jq .` returns OK on control plane. Clients: some 503s in app logs at 14:03.

ben (sre): paste logs: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:59Z proxy[pid=42] INFO route=embed req_id=abc123 latency=812ms status=200
2026-03-15T14:03:01Z proxy[pid=42] WARN route=gen req_id=def456 latency=905ms status=503
2026-03-15T14:03:05Z autoscaler INFO pool=dedicated-gpu action=scale_up delta=2 target=6
2026-03-15T14:03:11Z autoscaler INFO pool=dedicated-gpu action=scale_down delta=-2 target=4
```

ben (sre): looks like a very short scale-up then scale-down; KV cache warmup might have temporarily increased tail latency. Also saw one synthetic canary run at 14:02 that had a heavy prompt. Could be synthetic noise triggering the alert.

dave (support): any signs of customer-visible errors? Any SEV tickets?

alice (oncall): quick sweep of support queue — nothing urgent raised. No billing or demo flows showing failures. Telemetry shows small increase in error-rate for that minute but dropped back to baseline. No customer sessions impacted for >5m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC12345 auto-resolved (no ack required) — reason: alert threshold cleared.

alice (oncall): marking as transient. I'll do a short postmortem blurb and open a follow-up ticket to tune alerts. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) add a short cooldown to that proxy p95 alert (e.g., 5/10m window) 2) add synthetic-canary tag to synthetic tests so they don't trigger production latency alerts 3) check autoscaler stabilization policy.

carol (platform): agree on canary tagging. Also we should check kernel metrics on infer nodes — scheduling jitter can amplify KV cache warmup. Filing infra ticket.

ben (sre): quick command I ran to validate recent autoscaler ops: `kubectl get hpa --namespace=redwood -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, cpu:.status.currentCPUUtilizationPercentage, replicas:.status.currentReplicas}'` — output shows transient CPU bump then back down.

alice (oncall): no customer impact, SLOs unaffected. I'll hand off to ben for root-cause follow-up. Ben, please own the follow-up and add remediation/action items. Tag me when done. :white_check_mark:

ben (sre): will do. My next steps: correlate canary job run IDs with scale events, validate whether canary should be excluded from production alerts, and propose alert-window changes. Expect a short ticket within 1 business day.

dave (support): thanks — I'll note in the incident log that support monitored and no customer reports.

alice (oncall): closing thread for now, leaving follow-up ticket link once created. Good catch on rapid autoscale bounce — we should avoid noisy PD churn. :pray:

incident-bot: thread closed (root incident auto-resolved).
